cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where user-controlled data is embedded into HTML, attributes, JavaScript, or CSS contexts without proper context-aware escaping, leading to cross-site scripting. The root causes include incomplete HTML entity encoding, missing script-context escaping for JSON, confusion between text and HTML sinks, and lack of dedicated escaping for different contexts.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Add missing escape cases for attribute-specific characters or apply full HTML entity encoding (e.g., escape & < > ' " ) to all string values before HTML insertion..

sub_patterns.name: Incomplete HTML entity escaping for attribute and general HTML contexts
sub_patterns.root_cause: The HTML escaper omitted characters that are special in attribute values (single quote, equals, backtick) or HTML entity encoding was entirely missing for JSON string values inserted into HTML.
